slides.title: What is ASDLC?
slides.text: What is ASDLC? A development methodology where specs drive every decision Designed for human-agent collaboration, not just human teams Specs are living documents — blueprint + contract in one artifact Agents read specs before writing code, just like engineers should Eliminates ambiguity that causes LLM drift and hallucination

slides.title: The Workflow
slides.text: The Workflow Spec → Plan → Implement → Verify → Ship ↺ Ship feeds back into Spec Each arrow reads "is followed by": a phase's output is the next phase's input. Shipping updates the spec, so the cycle repeats. The spec is both the starting point and the acceptance gate.

slides.title: Spec as Contract
slides.text: Spec as Contract # feature-name.spec.md ## Blueprint - Architecture decisions and constraints - API surface and data flow - Anti-patterns to avoid ## Contract - Definition of Done checklist - Regression guardrails ### Scenarios Given a valid slide container When the user presses ArrowRight Then the next slide becomes active And the live region announces the change

slides.title: Benefits
slides.text: Benefits Deterministic agent output — specs constrain what gets built Auditable decisions — every choice traces to a spec section Testable by default — Gherkin scenarios map directly to tests Human-agent handoff — either party can pick up from the spec Drift protection — verify phase catches spec-code divergence
&fleur; Specs are the source of truth. asdlc.io

slides.title: Agentic software development lifecycle
slides.text: Agentic software development lifecycle A pattern library for building software with agents. People design and govern the system. Agents carry out the work.

slides.title: Three layers of agentic work
slides.text: Three layers of agentic work ASDLC’s three layers and the human role in each Layer Function Human role Context The supply chain—requirements, schemas, specs delivered just-in-time Editor Agents The logistics layer—moving information, generating code, running tests Operator Gates Quality control—deterministic checks + human oversight Governor

slides.title: Keep the state. Name the change.
slides.text: Keep the state. Name the change. The Spec STATE · LIVES WITH THE CODE The feature’s design and quality contract, kept current as the system changes. ## Blueprint Context, architecture, constraints ## Contract Done criteria, guardrails, scenarios Illustrative outline The PBI DELTA · CLOSED AFTER MERGE One scoped change, pointing to the spec and its verification criteria. A Product Backlog Item sets the task’s boundaries and how discoveries will be handled. When a change alters the contract, update the spec with it. Specs capture intent and constraints. Code remains authoritative for runtime logic.

slides.title: Different checks. Different questions.
slides.text: Different checks. Different questions. Quality DETERMINISTIC Does it compile and pass tests? Toolchain checks: types, lint, tests and build. Review PROBABILISTIC Does it satisfy the spec’s contracts? AI-assisted review of meaning, constraints and edge cases. Acceptance HUMAN JUDGMENT Is it the right thing? Usability, visual balance and strategic fit. ASDLC’s Context Gates pattern is marked Experimental.

slides.title: Try one bounded change
slides.text: Try one bounded change Spec PBI Implementation Gate Merge The introductory loop from ASDLC’s Getting Started guide. Give the agent the relevant context and a clear outcome to work toward. Review the evidence before accepting the change. Keep the spec current as the work teaches you more.
